newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares rise as political crisis eases.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares rise as political crisis eases.

text.p: Delhi shares posted early gains on Friday, boosted by expectations of an end to the nation's political crisis and anticipated strong results by Reliance Industries, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index was up 2.02 points at 771.90 after 30 minutes of trade.
"Hopes that the United Front might manage to elect an acceptable leader fuelled buying activity," Manmohan Sharma of stockbrokers Portfolio Management said.
Caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front coalition was set to meet at 9:30 p.m. (1600 GMT) on Friday to try to select a new leader.

The United Front said on Friday that Congress president Sitaram Kesri had withdrawn a March 31 letter staking a claim to power, lifting a crucial obstacle in the way of choosing a new United Front leader.
Reliance rose 2.10 rupees to 284 as speculators banking on strong results, due to be announced on April 22, snapped up shares.
State Bank of India gained 1.60 rupees to 298.85, boosted by the central bank's half-yearly credit policy.
Most of India's leading stock exchanges were closed on Friday for the Moslem holiday of Id al-Adha.
